_comment: Safety rail: responder.py will refuse to freeze anything matching these. Match by process NAME and/or resolved EXE PATH, not just PID, since PIDs are reused. Add your shell, IDE, debugger, and any process that legitimately touches the canary dir (e.g. baseline.py, monitor.py themselves) here.
notes: protected_pids should really only ever contain PID 1 (init) as a hardcoded floor. Everything else is matched dynamically at freeze-time via process name and cmdline, since hardcoding PIDs of your own tools is fragile across restarts.
